His brother
Pharaoh

answers: Joseph’s servants
The physicians
The Egyptians

answers: Forty days
Thirty days
Seventy days

He immediately left Egypt
He called all his brothers

To preserve the body after death
To mourn

Forty days were for the journey, and seventy days were for the burial

To describe two stages of the burial journey
To say that embalming lasted seventy days

The people of Egypt also joined in mourning him
Israel mourned for Egypt

The physicians
Israel

paragraphs.title: Joseph Asks to Leave and Bury His Father

easy.question: Who asked permission to bury his father in the land of Canaan?
answers: Joseph
Pharaoh
Pharaoh’s household
easy.explanation: Joseph asked to go up to the land of Canaan and bury his father there.

easy.question: Where did Joseph ask to bury his father?
answers: In Egypt
In the land of Canaan
In Pharaoh’s palace
easy.explanation: Joseph said that his father had made him swear to bury him in a grave in the land of Canaan.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh answer Joseph?
answers: You may not leave
Bury him in Egypt
Go up and bury your father
easy.explanation: Pharaoh gave Joseph permission to go up and bury his father as he had sworn to do.

medium.question: What did Joseph do after the days of mourning for his father had passed?
answers: He approached Pharaoh’s household with a request
He immediately left Egypt
He built a new tomb in Egypt
medium.explanation: After the mourning period, Joseph asked Pharaoh’s household to speak to Pharaoh about the burial.

medium.question: What does “found grace in your eyes” mean in the phrase “If now I have found grace in your eyes”?
answers: If they found the tomb
If I am acceptable to you
If the mourning period has ended
medium.explanation: The phrase comes before a request and means that Joseph asks them to regard him favorably and help him.

medium.question: Why did Joseph ask to go up to the land of Canaan?
answers: To visit his brothers
To find work
To bury his father
medium.explanation: Joseph explained that his father had made him swear to bury him in a grave in the land of Canaan.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Pharaoh’s words, “according as he made thee swear”?

Pharaoh thought Joseph had promised nothing
Pharaoh required Joseph to remain in Egypt
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh approved the request because it was connected to the oath Joseph had made to his father.

challenge.question: What does Joseph’s wording, “I will come again,” show about his intention?

He intended to return to Egypt after the burial
He wanted to move to another land
challenge.explanation: Joseph said that after going up and burying his father, he planned to return to Egypt.

challenge.question: Why did Joseph first approach “the house of Pharaoh” rather than ask Pharaoh directly?
answers: Because Pharaoh was not in Egypt
Because Joseph did not want to bury his father
Because he asked them to convey his request to Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: Joseph asked the members of Pharaoh’s household to speak in Pharaoh’s ears, meaning to pass his request on to him.

answers: Joseph
Pharaoh
Only his brothers
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Joseph went up to bury his father.”

easy.question: What did they leave in the land of Goshen?
answers: The weapons
Their little ones, flocks, and herds
The elders of Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that only the little ones, flocks, and herds were left in the land of Goshen.

easy.question: Who went up with Joseph besides his family?
answers: Only shepherds
Only the people of Goshen
Chariots and horsemen
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen.”

medium.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Joseph went to bury his father, and many people went up with him
The horsemen remained in Goshen, and only the children left
Joseph returned to Egypt, and afterward his father left
medium.explanation: First Joseph went to bury his father, and then the passage describes who went up with him.

medium.question: What does “their little ones” mean in the sentence “only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen”?
answers: Their elders
Their young children
Their soldiers
medium.explanation: “Their little ones” refers to their young children, who were left in Goshen along with the flocks and herds.

medium.question: What does the phrase “both chariots and horsemen” show about the procession?
answers: It was small and quiet
Everyone remained in the land of Goshen
It included a large and varied military escort
medium.explanation: Chariots and horsemen formed part of a military escort, showing why the company was very great.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that only the little ones, flocks, and herds remained in Goshen?
answers: Most of the adults and household members went on the journey
Joseph did not go on the journey
All the Egyptians remained in Goshen
challenge.explanation: The word “only” shows that just the children and animals remained, while the other household members left.

challenge.question: What does “it was a very great company” mean in this context?
answers: The people carried only heavy loads
The procession was very large and impressive
The journey stopped because the chariots were too heavy
challenge.explanation: Here, “great” describes the size and number of people in the procession, not merely physical weight.

Joseph went to bury his father

easy.question: Where did Joseph and his brothers mourn for Jacob?

In the cave of Machpelah
In Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that they came to the threshing floor of Atad and mourned there.

easy.question: How many days did the mourning for Jacob last?
answers: Three days
Seven days
Forty days
easy.explanation: The passage says, “he made a mourning for his father seven days.”

answers: The inhabitants of Canaan
The Egyptians
His sons
easy.explanation: The verse says, “For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan.”

medium.question: What did Jacob’s sons do after mourning for him?
answers: They buried him in the cave of Machpelah
They returned him to Egypt
They remained at the threshing floor of Atad
medium.explanation: After the mourning, his sons carried Jacob to Canaan and buried him in the cave of Machpelah.

medium.question: What does “mourning” mean in the phrase “they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation”?
answers: A long journey
Weeping and grief for the dead
A festive meal
medium.explanation: Mourning means grieving and weeping for someone who has died; here it describes the great grief for Jacob.

answers: Because Jacob was buried there
Because the place was inside Egypt
Because the Canaanites saw the Egyptians’ deep mourning
medium.explanation: The inhabitants of the land saw the Egyptians’ great mourning and therefore gave the place that name.

answers: It was a burial possession Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite
It was Joseph’s palace
It was the place of mourning at the threshing floor of Atad
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes that Abraham bought the field and cave from Ephron the Hittite as a burial possession.

challenge.question: Who returned to Egypt after Jacob’s burial?
answers: Joseph alone
Joseph, his brothers, and everyone who had gone up with him
Only the people of Canaan

Mourning at Atad, burial in Canaan, return to Egypt

answers: Joseph might take revenge on them
Joseph would leave Egypt
Joseph would praise them
easy.explanation: The brothers feared that Joseph would repay them for the evil they had done to him.

easy.question: What did the brothers ask Joseph to do?
answers: Give them money
Forgive them
Send them to the land of Canaan
easy.explanation: The brothers asked Joseph to forgive their trespass and sin.

easy.question: What did the brothers do at the end of the passage?
answers: They fled from Joseph
They wept before Joseph
They fell before Joseph and said they would be his servants
easy.explanation: The verse says that they fell down before Joseph and offered to be his servants.

medium.question: Why did the brothers fear that Joseph would harm them after their father’s death?
answers: Because Joseph was angry that they had not come to Egypt
Because they remembered the evil they had done to him
Because their father had commanded Joseph to punish them
medium.explanation: The brothers feared that Joseph would take revenge because of the evil they had done to him in the past.

medium.question: What does “hate us” mean in the phrase “Joseph will peradventure hate us”?
answers: Remember us favorably
Send us on our way
Hate us and hold a grudge against us
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means that Joseph might hate them or continue to resent them.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events in this passage?
answers: The brothers were afraid, approached Joseph, and he wept
Joseph wept, the brothers left Egypt, and then approached him
The brothers fell before Joseph, and then their father died
medium.explanation: First the brothers were afraid, then they sent their request to Joseph, and Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

They announced that they were already Pharaoh’s servants
They asked Joseph to work for them

To ask Joseph to leave Egypt
To appeal to their father’s wishes and seek reconciliation and forgiveness
challenge.explanation: They presented the request for forgiveness as their father’s command in an effort to soften Joseph’s attitude toward them.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “they did unto thee evil” show about how the brothers viewed their actions?

They claimed that Joseph had harmed them
They said that nothing had happened between them

Leave Egypt
Give me back my money
easy.explanation: Joseph said to his brothers, “Fear not,” so that they would not be afraid of him.

easy.question: What did the brothers intend to do to Joseph?
answers: Do him a kindness
Do him evil
Return him to Canaan
easy.explanation: Joseph said to his brothers, “Ye thought evil against me.”

easy.question: Whom did Joseph promise to care for?
answers: Only himself
Only the king of Egypt
His brothers and their children
easy.explanation: Joseph promised, “I will nourish you, and your little ones.”

medium.question: How did what the brothers intended to do to Joseph become something good?
answers: Their action helped save many people from famine
Joseph completely forgot his brothers
The brothers became kings of Egypt
medium.explanation: Joseph said that although the brothers intended evil, God meant it for good in order to save many people.

medium.question: What does “I will nourish you” mean in this context?
answers: I will punish you
I will provide for and care for you
I will hide you
medium.explanation: Joseph was promising to provide food and care for his brothers and their children.

medium.question: What did Joseph do after promising to provide for his brothers and their children?
answers: He immediately sent them out of Egypt
He asked them to fight
He comforted them and spoke kindly to them
medium.explanation: The passage says that Joseph comforted them and spoke kindly to them.

challenge.question: What does Joseph’s question, “Am I in the place of God?” show about his attitude?
answers: He did not want revenge and left judgment to God
He thought that he was God
He intended to leave Egypt
challenge.explanation: Joseph emphasized that he was not in God’s place to judge and take revenge, so he chose to reassure his brothers.

The brothers intended evil, but God turned the result toward good
The brothers did nothing, and everything happened by chance

Because they wanted to leave the family
Because they feared that Joseph would take revenge on them
challenge.explanation: The repeated reassurance and promise to provide for them show that the brothers feared punishment or revenge.

answers: In Egypt
In Canaan
In Midian
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father’s house.”

easy.question: How old was Joseph when he died?
answers: One hundred years old
One hundred and ten years old
One hundred and twenty years old
easy.explanation: The passage says that Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.

easy.question: What did the Egyptians do to Joseph’s body after his death?
answers: They buried him immediately in Canaan
They burned him
They embalmed him and placed him in a coffin
easy.explanation: The passage says, “They embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.”

medium.question: Why did Joseph make the children of Israel swear to carry up his bones?
answers: Because he believed that God would bring them out of Egypt to the Promised Land
Because he did not want to be buried in Egypt
Because he wanted the Israelites to remain in Egypt
medium.explanation: Joseph connected the oath with God’s promise to bring the children of Israel to the land sworn to their fathers.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Joseph died, then spoke with his brothers, and finally made them swear
Joseph spoke about leaving the land, made the children of Israel swear, and then died
The Israelites carried Joseph’s bones up, and then Joseph died
medium.explanation: First Joseph spoke of God’s future visitation, then he made the Israelites swear, and finally he died and was embalmed.

medium.question: What does “they embalmed him” mean in the sentence “they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin”?
answers: They prayed over him
They carried him to another land
They preserved his body after death
medium.explanation: The context describes what was done to Joseph’s body after his death, so embalming means preserving the body.

Joseph saw Ephraim when he was thirty years old
Joseph lived only thirty years after Ephraim
challenge.explanation: The statement says that Joseph saw Ephraim’s descendants to the third generation, emphasizing his long life and the continuation of the family.

Joseph’s death would not cancel God’s promise of deliverance and bringing them to the land
Joseph told the Israelites to leave Egypt immediately
challenge.explanation: Joseph says that he will die but emphasizes that God will continue to act and bring the Israelites out of Egypt in the future.

challenge.question: What does the repetition in “God will surely visit you” emphasize?
answers: That God had briefly forgotten the Israelites
That Joseph was unsure whether God would act
The certainty that God would remember the Israelites and act for them
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording emphasizes the certainty and importance of God’s future action in bringing Israel out of Egypt.
